subject: bed pillow
title: What If You Never Replaced Your Pillow?

scenes.text: What if you never replaced your pillow? It won't double in weight. The truth is weirder.
Every night you shed skin flakes and sweat into it, food for microscopic dust mites.
Some estimates say mites and their droppings can make up a tenth of an old pillow's weight.
In 2005, scientists tested 10 old pillows and found 4 to 16 kinds of fungus in each one.
A common mold called Aspergillus was in every single pillow, synthetic ones worst of all.
Meanwhile the filling flattens. Experts say replace it every one to two years, before your neck notices.

description:
What if you never replaced your pillow? The claim that pillows or mattresses double in weight from dust mites has no scientific support, but by some estimates mites and their droppings can make up about 10% of an old pillow's weight.
A University of Manchester study of 10 pillows aged 1.5 to 20 years found 4 to 16 fungal species in each, with Aspergillus fumigatus in all of them. Most experts recommend replacing pillows every 1 to 2 years.
